After a write exits 128, the tool reads git's stderr and repeats the write only when it holds git's lock-file text (the `Unable to create '….lock': File exists` form that a held index, `HEAD`, or ref lock prints); every other exit 128 is passed on at once as one `Error:` line after its single attempt. Git is run with a fixed C locale so the message is not translated. After a write exits 128, the tool reads git's stderr and stops at once only when it matches a short stated list of failures no lock causes (starting with `pathspec '…' did not match any files`); every other exit 128, an unrecognized message included, is repeated on the present schedule. After a write exits 128, the tool reads no message text but checks git's own lock files, resolved through `git rev-parse --git-path` (the index lock, `HEAD.lock`, and the current branch's ref lock): it repeats the write while one of them exists, repeats it once more when none exists so a lock released between the failure and the probe is still absorbed, and passes on a further 128 with no lock file present after that second attempt. The tool gains file probes and a branch on what git keeps under its directory, a lock it does not probe (another ref, a packed-refs or config lock) is treated as a non-lock after two attempts, and the retry test must hold each probed lock file, so the mechanics grow more than a message match would.
